milestone: M28 Headless Patch Recovery Apply Continuation

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Headless callers can cross the patch recovery proposal review boundary by applying one already-approved recovery proposal through a replay-safe continuation.
The continuation delegates actual mutation to existing Rust-owned proposal.apply and adds no separate mutation policy.
Rust runtime rejects stale progress, missing authorization, stale M27 source/recovery/proposal provenance, unsafe proposal scope, and bad fingerprints before apply delegation.
Continuation decisions record bounded IDs, fingerprints, apply handles, route intent, and replay evidence without raw file, hunk, diff, prompt, provider, command, environment, or path data.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting controlled_workspace_tools, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.continue_once can apply one approved patch apply recovery proposal through existing proposal.apply and return bounded replay-safe apply metadata.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Direct proposal.apply can mutate safely, but it requires caller-owned route switching after M27.2 proposal review and does not persist one headless continuation decision for this recovery apply boundary.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Patch recovery remains stuck at review/authorize proposal for long-running headless callers, and lost responses around direct proposal.apply remain caller-owned.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M27.1 admitted recovery, M27.1.1 hardened exact-source binding, and M27.2 ran recovery to proposal review. M28.1 applies the already-approved recovery proposal.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing headless.continue_once parameters and reuses existing proposal.apply.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It returns existing bounded ProposalApplyResult metadata and a bounded next route; no readiness/report/history/digest/preview/inspection surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: A valid continuation performs exactly one controlled patch_file apply through the existing Rust-owned apply path and replays without duplicate apply or continuation evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can continue recover -> run -> review -> approved apply without switching to caller-owned apply orchestration.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the core M28 boundary from approved patch recovery proposal to bounded apply result if post-apply progress routing remains compatible.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts patch_apply_recovery_apply_target for one approved recovery-scoped patch_file proposal and delegates mutation to proposal.apply
valid continuation mutates exactly one existing UTF-8 file through existing controlled patch_file apply gates
stale progress, missing authorization, mismatched source/recovery/proposal provenance, non-recovery proposal scope, and invalid fingerprints fail before apply delegation
replay with the same continuation_id returns the same bounded apply result without duplicate WorkspacePatchApplyResultRecorded or HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded evidence
existing proposal.apply failure behavior is preserved for expected target hash or preflight failures
VSIX protocol validation accepts only bounded patch recovery apply target fields and rejects raw prompt/file/content/path fields
no new RPC, readiness/report/history/digest/preview/inspection-only endpoint, automatic approval, automatic apply, duplicated mutation policy, or raw data exposure is introduced

next_phase_candidate_notes: After M28.1 lands, assess M28 closeout. Do not add another apply wrapper/status phase; plan follow-up only for a distinct post-apply execution boundary if existing progress/retry routing cannot consume the bounded apply result.
